summary.text: Male neonate born at 38 weeks and six days with hydrops fetalis and hematological disorders; the pregnancy was complicated by maternal nicotine use and anemia.

Examination showed abdominal distension, hepatomegaly, pallor, petechiae and dependent edema, with symptoms appearing within the first 24 hours of life. Laboratory tests showed anemia, thrombocytopenia and leukocyte lineage rejuvenation; TORCH infections and neonatal lupus were excluded; echocardiography and MRI findings and a bone marrow biopsy were reported.
On the 21st day of life AML, specifically AMKL (M7), was diagnosed and bone marrow genetic analysis showed an SRP72 mutation.

summary.text: Male neonate born by cesarean section at 38 weeks of gestation with suspected congenital hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice and thrombocytopenia; his mother had a mild respiratory infection in the third trimester. Apgar score was 10 and weight 3040 grams.

Examination showed hepatosplenomegaly, jaundice with high conjugated bilirubin from the first day, petechiae and episodes of bradycardia; blood tests showed severe thrombocytopenia and elevated liver enzymes. He received phototherapy, ampicillin and gentamicin for seven days, seven platelet transfusions, and ursodeoxycholic acid, fat-soluble vitamins and phenobarbital for cholestasis.

Hereditary spherocytosis, hemophagocytic syndrome, red blood cell enzyme defects and galactosemia were excluded. AMKL was diagnosed on the 26th day of life after bone marrow aspiration and trephine biopsy; whole-exome sequencing of blast cells showed four autosomal trisomies (chromosomes 14, 15, 19 and 21) and no disease-causing single-nucleotide variants. He was transferred to the pediatric hematology department.

summary.text: Full-term female newborn (40 weeks, 2800 g, Apgar 10) born after a pregnancy complicated by maternal gestational diabetes mellitus and a viral infection; the mother tested positive for COVID-19 on the 10th day postpartum and carries the factor V Leiden mutation. She was admitted on the 14th day of life for thrombocytopenia.

She had hepatosplenomegaly and signs of an upper respiratory tract infection, pancytopenia, hyperferritinemia, hypofibrinogenemia and elevated soluble CD25, raising a strong suspicion of HLH; CT showed hepatomegaly with heterogeneous liver parenchyma. HLH-2004 treatment with dexamethasone, tocilizumab, IVIG and etoposide was stopped after severe neutropenia and no improvement; congenital HLH was not confirmed.

Bone marrow biopsy on the 17th day showed numerous blasts consistent with megakaryoblasts; AMKL (M7) was diagnosed on the 38th day of life and AML-BFM 2017 treatment was started. She then developed desaturation, edema, metabolic acidosis, sepsis due to Stenotrophomonas maltophilia and other complications, was transferred to the intensive care unit, and died.
